episode.title: Replace a text-producing shortcut with a modifier-only chord
episode.before: At parent cd83e73845f2304791c782741d42d7354a32053c, the plan-mode extension registered Shift+P as the shortcut for toggling plan mode. The terminal key matcher treats Shift plus a letter as the uppercase form of that letter, so the shortcut overlapped with ordinary capital-P text input. The extension comment and README also advertised Shift+P.
episode.after: At 39ee5fee92c5c4c004fb117382411487ed30fadc, the same toggle handler is registered with Ctrl+Alt+P through the existing typed key helper. The implementation comment and README advertise Ctrl+Alt+P. The command-based /plan toggle and the toggle behavior are unchanged.
episode.diff: The implementation replaces Key.shift("p") with Key.ctrlAlt("p") at the plan-mode shortcut registration while retaining the description and handler. Two documentation references are changed from Shift+P to Ctrl+Alt+P, and the coding-agent changelog records that the replacement avoids conflict with typing capital P. No test file was added or modified.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 39ee5fee identifies the defect as Shift+P conflicting with typing capital P and selects Ctrl+Alt+P while avoiding Ctrl+Shift+P and Shift+Alt+P conflicts.
The parent implementation registers the plan-mode toggle as pi.registerShortcut(Key.shift("p"), ...) and invokes togglePlanMode from its handler.
The resolved implementation registers the same description and togglePlanMode handler with Key.ctrlAlt("p").
The behavioral code diff changes only the registered key identifier from Key.shift("p") to Key.ctrlAlt("p"); the shortcut handler remains the plan-mode toggle.
Extension shortcut dispatch iterates registered shortcuts, passes each identifier to matchesKey, invokes the matching handler, and consumes the input.
The typed key API supports Ctrl+Alt combinations: Key.ctrlAlt constructs a ctrl+alt key identifier, and matchesKey combines Ctrl and Alt modifier bits before matching letter input.
The key matcher recognizes Shift plus a letter from uppercase legacy input, establishing why Shift+P overlaps with ordinary capital-P entry.
The extension runner normalizes registered shortcut identifiers, rejects built-in reserved conflicts, and exposes accepted shortcuts for interactive dispatch.
The plan-mode source comment and README are updated from Shift+P to Ctrl+Alt+P, keeping user-facing shortcut guidance aligned with registration.

Repository inspection confirms that no test file changed in the resolution commit; validation evidence for this episode is therefore limited to the existing typed key/matching contract and static before/after inspection, not a new shortcut regression test or recorded runtime check.
The changelog records that the plan-mode example shortcut changed to avoid conflict with typing capital P.

candidate_atomics.name: replace-text-producing-shortcut-with-modifier-chord
candidate_atomics.title: Replace a text-producing shortcut with a non-text chord
candidate_atomics.description: Rebind an existing action from a shifted printable letter that collides with normal text entry to a supported multi-modifier chord, without changing the action handler.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent ordinary capital-letter input from unintentionally activating an application action while preserving keyboard access to that action.
semantic_action.module_role: Interactive shortcut registration and dispatch boundary
semantic_action.pre_state: An action is registered on Shift plus a printable letter, and the input matcher also recognizes the corresponding uppercase character as that shortcut.
semantic_action.post_state: The action retains its handler but is registered on a supported modifier chord that does not overlap with ordinary capital-letter entry or the documented neighboring conflicts.
semantic_action.validation: Compare the parent and resolved registrations to confirm only the key identifier changed; verify the replacement identifier is accepted by the typed key API and dispatched through the existing matcher. Runtime conflict testing remains unrecorded.

candidate_atomics.title: Synchronize user-facing shortcut guidance
candidate_atomics.description: Update source guidance, usage documentation, and change notes so users see the same shortcut that the application registers.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure that discoverable shortcut instructions agree with the implemented registration after rebinding.
semantic_action.pre_state: Comments and usage documentation advertise the old conflicting shortcut.
semantic_action.post_state: Comments, usage documentation, and change notes identify the replacement chord used by the implementation.
semantic_action.validation: Diff the registration and all changed shortcut references and confirm they name Ctrl+Alt+P consistently.

candidate_workflows.name: resolve-printable-key-shortcut-conflict
candidate_workflows.title: Resolve a shortcut that intercepts ordinary text input
candidate_workflows.description: Trace a reported text-entry collision to shortcut matching semantics, replace the binding without changing its action, and reconcile all advertised shortcut references.

workflow_graph.goal: Ordinary printable input no longer activates the application action, while the action remains available through a supported and consistently documented shortcut.
when_to_use: A shortcut based on Shift plus a printable letter is triggered by ordinary uppercase text input.
The shortcut system supports a distinguishable multi-modifier chord and exposes reserved bindings for conflict checks.
anti_goals: Do not change the action's behavior, state transition, or command-based activation path.
Do not modify the global key parser when the conflict is caused by an individual binding choice.
Do not select a replacement solely because it is syntactically valid; account for built-in and common platform conflicts.
not_applicable_when: The observed event is incorrectly normalized by the input parser rather than correctly matching an unsuitable registered binding.
The target environment cannot distinguish the proposed modifier chord.
The action handler itself, rather than shortcut selection, causes the unintended behavior.
inputs: The conflicting shortcut registration and its action handler
Key-event matching semantics for printable letters and modifiers
Known platform or tool shortcuts near the proposed replacement
workflow_graph.entry_state: A shifted printable-letter binding shares an input representation with normal uppercase text and can invoke an action during typing.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The unchanged action handler is registered on a supported, non-text-producing chord, and user-facing references agree with the new binding.

steps.condition: The reported collision is confirmed by the matcher treating uppercase letter input as Shift plus that letter, and a non-reserved replacement chord is available.
steps.validation: The parent/resolved diff preserves the handler while changing the key identifier; the key API constructs and matcher accepts the replacement chord.

steps.condition: Source comments, usage documentation, or change records expose the shortcut to users.
steps.validation: Every changed user-facing reference names the same chord as the resolved registration.

validation_ladder: Confirm the before-state collision from the parent registration and the matcher branch that maps uppercase input to Shift plus a letter.
Confirm the replacement chord is representable by the typed key API and is not rejected by the extension runner's reserved-shortcut check.
Confirm shortcut dispatch still reaches the unchanged action handler.
Confirm comments and usage documentation match the implemented chord.
Add or run a focused input-dispatch regression test where available; this episode contains no new or recorded runtime test.
stop_conditions: Stop if the collision cannot be reproduced or established from key-matching semantics.
Stop if the proposed chord is reserved, indistinguishable in supported terminals, or conflicts with required platform behavior.
Defer completion if implementation and user-facing shortcut references disagree.
Do not claim runtime portability or regression coverage without an executed oracle.
unresolved_or_deferred: No changed test directly demonstrates that capital P remains text or that Ctrl+Alt+P toggles plan mode.
The commit message asserts cross-platform safety, but the available evidence bundle contains no platform matrix or runtime verification.
No GitHub review, status-check, issue-body, or comment evidence is available.

unresolved_questions: Was Ctrl+Alt+P manually verified across all supported terminal protocols and operating systems?
Should a focused regression test cover both non-activation on capital P and activation on Ctrl+Alt+P?
